secant.def: A straight line through two points on a curve; its gradient gives the average rate of change between those points.

derivative.def: An instantaneous rate of change, represented by the tangent gradient of a differentiable function.

limit.def: The value an expression approaches as an input approaches a specified value.

increasing.def: Describes a function whose values rise as its input rises over an interval.

decreasing.def: Describes a function whose values fall as its input rises over an interval.

stationary point.def: A point on a differentiable curve where the first derivative is zero; it need not be a turning point.

power rule.def: The differentiation rule that multiplies a power term by its exponent and reduces that exponent by one.

tangent.def: A line with the local direction of a differentiable curve at the contact point.

normal.def: A line perpendicular to the tangent at a specified point on a curve.

antiderivative.def: A function whose derivative is a given function.

indefinite integral.def: A family of antiderivatives written with an arbitrary additive constant.

definite integral.def: Signed accumulation of a function between specified lower and upper bounds.

chain rule.def: Differentiation of a composite function by multiplying the outer derivative by the inner derivative.

product rule.def: Differentiation of two multiplied functions by adding the derivative of each factor times the unchanged other factor.

quotient rule.def: Differentiation of a quotient using the difference of cross products divided by the denominator squared.

second derivative.def: The derivative of the first derivative, describing how a function’s slope changes.

concavity.def: The bending behaviour of a graph: concave up for increasing slopes and concave down for decreasing slopes.

local maximum.def: A point where the function value is at least as great as nearby values.

local minimum.def: A point where the function value is at least as small as nearby values.

optimisation.def: Finding the best permitted value of an objective within its domain and constraints.

point of inflexion.def: A point where a curve changes concavity; a zero second derivative alone does not prove this.

displacement.def: Signed change in position along a chosen direction.

velocity.def: The rate of change of displacement with time, including a sign for direction.

acceleration.def: The rate of change of velocity with time.

substitution.def: An integration method that replaces an inside expression with a new variable and transforms the differential accordingly.

fundamental theorem of calculus.def: The link between integration and differentiation that evaluates a definite integral by subtracting antiderivative values at the bounds.

geometric area.def: Nonnegative area of a region; unlike a signed integral, below-axis pieces contribute positively.
